name: gap_sector_leader_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When a sector leader gaps strongly (>0.8%), the lagging sector peers tend to catch up during the first 60-90 minutes as the same macro/sector catalyst that drove the leader's gap percolates through the sector. For example, if HDFCBANK gaps up 1.2%, KOTAKBANK and AXISBANK often follow with delayed moves. The leader's gap signals sector-wide information that the market hasn't fully priced into the laggers yet. The inefficiency exists because laggers have lower pre-open participation and their prices update slowly in the first 15-30 minutes. By buying laggers when the leader gaps, we capture the information transmission premium.
universe: Banking sector (HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK, AXISBANK, SBIN) on NSE
stock_filter: leader gap > 0.8%; laggers gapping < 0.3% (clear divergence); all must have volume > ₹100cr avg
indicators: leader_gap = max(abs(gap_pct) for stock in sector_basket)
leader_stock = argmax(abs(gap_pct) for stock in sector_basket)
lagger_gap = gap_pct for each non-leader stock

long.confirmation: lagger_close crosses above EMA_9 within first 30 mins of open

conditions: gap_spread > 0.5 (lagger under-gapping by >50bps in abs terms)
short.confirmation: lagger_close crosses below EMA_9 within first 30 mins

entry.entry_price: market order on the lagger stock at EMA_9 cross confirmation

exit.target: lagger catches up to 60% of leader's gap (gap_spread narrows to 40% of original)
exit.stop_loss: lagger moves against position by 0.3% from entry OR 0.5 * ATR_10
exit.trailing_stop: after 30% catch-up, trail stop at entry price (breakeven)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 60 mins (catch-up should happen in morning)
exit.signal_exit: if leader reverses its gap (leader_return_from_open < 0), exit lagger trade

filters.time_filter: enter between 09:20-10:00 IST; catch-up window is narrow
filters.volume_filter: leader must have opening 5-min volume > 2x average (confirming institutional flow)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_BANK gap same direction as leader (macro alignment)
filters.event_filter: leader gap must NOT be due to stock-specific news (earnings, M&A); must be sector/macro driven
other_filters: skip if lagger has stock-specific news that explains its under-gapping (divergence is justified)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — information transmission delays are structural to multi-stock sectors

weaknesses: The lagger may be under-gapping for a good reason (stock-specific headwind) that the filter doesn't catch, leading to the gap spread persisting or widening
Sector leader identification is based on gap size, but the largest gap may be a stock-specific event disguised as a sector move, causing the lagger trade to fail
Low frequency: the specific leader-gap > 0.8% with clear lagger under-gapping condition occurs only 3-5 times per month in banking sector
prior_art: Hou (2007) industry information diffusion; Cohen & Frazzini (2008) economic links and predictable returns. Indian banking sector adaptation for intraday leader-lagger dynamics.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 48bps - 0.40 * 28bps = 28.8 - 11.2 = 17.6bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.6bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~12.9bps daily. The 26bps estimate includes portfolio effects from occasionally trading 2 laggers simultaneously. Sector cohesion is higher in Indian banking than most other sectors.
